entries.subject: Size: JPL Small-Body Database diameter
entries.finding: 375 Ursula is drawn as a sphere at the 216 km diameter the JPL Small-Body Database lists, with JPL's stated reference Dunham occult. list: Millis et al. 1984a. DAMIT held no shape model for it on 2026-10-08, so the sphere is illustrative.

entries.subject: Ursula whole-disc color
entries.finding: Gaia Collaboration, Galluccio et al. (2023) published the mean of 15 Gaia epoch spectra of the unresolved disc: reflectance against the Sun in 16 bands from 374 to 1034 nm, 1 at 550 nm (0.951 at 462 nm, 1.003 at 638 nm). The sphere is painted in that one color (#373634 in sRGB) through the shared disc-integrated-color method, scaled to the 3.7% geometric albedo JPL lists (± 2%), from NEOWISE (Nugent et al. 2016, AJ 152, 63; PDS bundle neowise_diameters_albedos 2.0). It is one mean, not a map. Tinaut-Ruano et al. (2023), A&A 669, L14, found Gaia DR3 reflectances slightly too red at wavelengths shorter than 550 nm; the bands are used as published, without that paper's correction.
